name: cloudflare
description: Cloudflare Worker deploy module (optional static assets, Durable Object, Container)
instructions: Add CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN to packages/infra/environments/<env>/secrets.yaml; set accountId in the instance config (not a secret). Alternatively set `apiToken: { from, output }` to pull the deploy credential from an imported instance's outputs (e.g. a cloudflare-token instance's tokenValue) — then no CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN needs to sit in secrets.yaml, though environments that destroy workers (ephemeral previews) still need the secrets.yaml fallback at teardown. The Worker topology lives in the package's own wrangler.jsonc, which is the source of truth for it. For per-PR preview workers, set workerName (e.g. `zbc-<app>-pr-${process.env.PR_NUMBER}`) on the preview instance; use wranglerEnv to select a named `env.<name>` block in wrangler.jsonc instead. Container-backed Workers need Docker running locally at apply time and a Workers Paid plan with Containers enabled. workerSecrets/workerVars entries are either a plain name (from secrets.yaml) or `{ name, from, output }` to pull a value from an imported instance's outputs (the instance must also be listed in this instance's `imports`) — secrets are pushed via `wrangler secret put`, vars via `wrangler deploy --var`. Bindings (D1, KV, R2, Queues, Vectorize, …) take their identifier from `bindings`: `{ type: 'd1_databases', binding: 'DB', field: 'database_id', from: 'app-db', output: 'databaseId' }` — `type` is the wrangler config key holding the binding array (dotted for nested ones, `queues.producers`), `field` the key on the matched entry to set, and the value is that `{ from, output }` reference or a `value` literal. The binding must already be declared in the package's wrangler.jsonc; zbc only fills in the identifier. `r2Bindings` is the R2 shorthand for the same thing.
